claim_1.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of plasma from 212 vaccinated individuals across five influenza vaccine seasons showed a significant decrease in antibody responses with age in the 2010 and 2011 seasons compared to younger individuals.

sources.section: Antibody Responses to Influenza Vaccination Correlate with Age but Not Gender, Race, or Diabetic Status
sources.quote: In the 2010 and 2011 seasons, in which elderly subjects were included, antibody responses showed a significant decrease with age ( Figures 1B , 1C , and S1C ), consistent with previous studies ( Seidman et al., 2012 ).

comparison.finding: significant decrease in antibody responses with age in the 2010 and 2011 seasons compared to younger individuals

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects vaccinated with TIV showed that modules related to interferon response and activation of dendritic cells were enriched on days 1 and 3 after vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells were negatively associated with the antibody response compared to baseline.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells ( Figures 2A and 2B ) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.

comparison.finding: modules related to interferon response and activation of dendritic cells were enriched on day 1
modules related to interferon response and activation of dendritic cells were enriched on day 3
